page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel x86_64 processor featuring 8 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is delivered via a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, representing a 0.3333 allocation with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14175.12. Memory bandwidth reaches 784.94 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 88.57 GB/sec for large-block reads. However, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks. For a small 135M model, it achieves prompt processing speeds of 9944.32 tokens/sec and text generation speeds of 464.42 tokens/sec. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 3147.67 tokens/sec and text generation at 107.73 tokens/sec.

The fractional GPU allocation offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not need a full, dedicated A40 GPU, reducing resource waste. A primary hardware tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and a moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits raw single-core compute performance, as reflected in the average stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68.

This server configuration is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, data analysis, and database operations. The combination of 16 GB VRAM, 40.0 GB system memory, and 740 GB NVMe SSD storage supports workloads such as running small-to-medium language models, batch data processing, and web serving applications.
